Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

Tabaraka (blessed): that is, its blessing has multiplied and encompassed all creation.

Alladhi nazzala al-furqan (He who sent down the Criterion): that is, Allah, who sent down the Qur'an as a criterion (furqan) distinguishing between truth and falsehood.

Ala 'abdihi (upon His servant): that is, Muhammad ﷺ.

Li-yakuna lil-'alamina nadhiran (that he may be a warner to the worlds): that is, that Muhammad ﷺ may be a warner to the worlds, of mankind and the jinn, warning them of Allah's punishment and chastisement if they disbelieve in Him and do not worship Him or affirm His oneness.

Faqaddarahu taqdiran (and He created everything and determined it precisely): that is, He fashioned it with a fashioning established on a foundation free of crookedness, with neither excess nor deficiency, in accordance with what wisdom and benefit require.

Darran wa la naf'an (any harm or benefit): that is, they have no power to repel harm or bring about benefit.

Mawtan wa la hayatan wa la nushuran (death, life, or resurrection): that is, they have no power to cause anyone to die, to give anyone life, or to raise the dead.

Meaning of the verses:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, praises Himself, saying that His goodness is great and His blessing has encompassed all creatures. He is the One who sent down the Criterion, the great Book by which He distinguishes truth from falsehood, monotheism from polytheism, justice from injustice. He sent it down upon His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ, so that he might be a warner to the worlds, to mankind and the jinn, warning them of the consequences of disbelief, polytheism, wrongdoing, evil and corruption, which are Allah's punishment and chastisement in this world and the Hereafter. His words ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ mean by creation, possession and servitude, and this is praise following praise. His words ﴿He has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and He created everything and determined it precisely﴾ are another great praise, in which He, blessed and exalted, praises Himself for His dominion, power, creation, knowledge and wisdom. His words ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods﴾ (idols) ﴿who create nothing, and are themselves created, and possess no power to benefit or harm themselves﴾, let alone others among their worshippers, ﴿any harm or benefit﴾, that is, they have no power to repel harm or bring about benefit, and they possess no power over death for anyone, nor life for another, nor resurrection of people on the Day of Judgment. Is this not a matter of wonder and astonishment? With Allah, whose blessing has encompassed the universe and who sent down the Criterion, the Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth, exalted above having a son or a partner, and high above that with great exaltation, and who created everything and determined it precisely, they take other gods, idols, which cannot repel harm from themselves, nor bring benefit to themselves, nor possess death, life, or resurrection. Glory be to Allah! Where do people's minds go? There is no power and no strength except with Allah.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The manifestations of Allah's lordship which necessitate His divinity: the outpouring of good upon creation, and dominion, power, knowledge and wisdom.

2- Denunciation of polytheism and polytheists.

3- Affirmation of monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and recompense.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ifk iftarahu* (a lie): that is, the Qur'an is nothing but a falsehood invented by Muhammad, and it is not the speech of God, Exalted is He. So they said.

*Zulman wa-zuran* (injustice and falsehood): that is, God answered their claim by saying that they came with injustice, since they made the miraculous speech that guides to happiness and human perfection into an invented lie, and with falsehood, by attributing to him what is innocent of it.

*Iktatabaha* (had it written): that is, he asked for it to be written for him, and it was written for him.

*Ya'lamu al-sirr* (He knows the secret): that is, He knows what the people of the heavens and the earth keep secret and what they conceal in their souls.

*Aw yulqa ilayhi kanz* (or a treasure be cast down to him): that is, from the heaven, so that he might spend from it and not need to go about in the markets.

*Jannatun ya'kulu minha* (a garden from which he eats): an orchard containing what suffices him of kinds of grain and fruit.

*Rajulan mashuran* (a man under sorcery): one who is deceived, his reason overpowered.

*Daraba lakal-amthal* (they have struck similitudes for you): that is, with sorcery, madness, poetry, soothsaying, lying, and the like.

*Fa-dallu fa-la yastatituna sabilan* (so they have strayed, and cannot find a way): they have strayed from the true path, which is that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, so they are not guided.

**The meaning of the verses:**

God informs us about those foolish idolaters who took, besides the Lord of the worlds, gods of idols that neither harm nor benefit. Beyond their folly in taking stones as gods to worship, they said of the noble Qur'an and the great Criterion (al-Furqan) that it is nothing but a lie (*ifk*), invented by Muhammad, and that other people, meaning the Jews, helped him to produce it. They uttered this detestable falsehood as an injustice (*zulm*) and a fabrication (*zur*). It was an injustice because they made the Qur'an, which is miraculous and carries guidance and light, into a lie, and they made the one innocent of lying, who had never lied at all, into a liar. Thus their saying about it was false and vain.

As for God's words: ﴿And they say: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ This verse was revealed in response to the devil of Quraysh, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who used to go to al-Hira and learn the stories of the kings of Persia and of Rustam. When Muhammad (ﷺ) warned his people that what had befallen the nations before them might befall them, and then rose from the assembly, he would come and sit down and say, "Come, let me relate to you; I tell a better story than Muhammad." He claimed that what Muhammad said was among the lies and myths of the storytellers (*qussas*) that they had written down in their books; he would recount them, and they were dictated to him, meaning that someone else dictated them to him morning and evening. God answered this slander by saying to His Messenger: ﴿Say: "He has sent it down who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth."﴾ That is, the Qur'an was sent down by Him who knows what the people of the heavens and the earth keep secret. He is the Knower of the unseen, who has knowledge of hearts and the knower of inner secrets. Had His mercy not preceded His wrath, He would have destroyed whoever disbelieved in Him and associated others with Him. ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ He covers the lapses of whoever repents to Him and shows mercy to him, however great his sins.

And God's words: ﴿And they say: "What is this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why has not an angel been sent down to him to be a warner with him, or a treasure cast down to him, or a garden for him from which he may eat?" And the wrongdoers say: "You follow none but a man under sorcery."﴾ These are the words of the chiefs and leaders of Quraysh, when they proposed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he abandon his call to his Lord in exchange for whatever he wished of kingship, wealth, women, or status, and he refused all of that. They then said to him: "Then take for yourself what you want, since why, when you are the Messenger of God, do you eat food and walk in the markets seeking a livelihood like us? Ask your Lord to send an angel down to you so that he may be a warner with you, or to cast down to you a treasure of gold and silver with which you may live as the richest of men, or to give you a garden of palms and grapes, or to give you palaces of gold by which you may be distinguished from the people, and your rank will be recognized, and you will be master over your people."

As for God's words: ﴿And the wrongdoers said﴾, that is, to the believers among the Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿You follow none but a man under sorcery﴾, meaning that by following Muhammad in what he has brought and calls to, you follow only a man under sorcery, that is, one deceived and overpowered in his reason, who does not know what he says or what he does. So leave him, and do not part from what your fathers and your people are upon.

As for God's words: ﴿Look how they strike similitudes for you, so they have strayed and cannot find a way.﴾ That is: Look, O Our Messenger, at these deluded idolaters, how they have framed for you false likenesses and struck false similitudes. They called you at one time a sorcerer, at another a poet, a soothsayer, and a madman. They were lost in these conjectures and strayed from the path of truth, so no guidance is hoped for them any more. This is because their error is so deep that they cannot return to the truth, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿so they cannot find a way.﴾

2. Affirmation of divine revelation and of the prophethood of Muhammad.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 10–16:

Explanation of the words:

Tabaraka (تبارك): That is, He is sanctified, His good is abundant, and His blessing is widespread.

Khayran min dhalika (خيراً من ذلك): That is, better than what the polytheists proposed to you.

Wa yaj'al laka qusuran (ويجعل لك قصوراً): That is, many palaces, not a single palace as the polytheists said.

Bal kadhdhabu bis-sa'ah (بل كذبوا بالساعة): That is, what prevented them from believing was not that you eat food and walk in the markets; rather, their denial of the Resurrection and the Recompense is the cause of that.

Taghayyudhan wa zafiran (تغيظاً وزفيراً): That is, a frightful sound from its rage against its people, the polytheists who disbelieved in Allah.

Muqarranin (مقرنين): That is, their hands are bound together with their necks in shackles.

Da'aw hunalika thubura (دعوا هنالك ثبوراً): That is, they call out, "Woe to us!" meaning "Our destruction!", for thubur means destruction.

Kanat lahum jaza'an wa masira (كانت لهم جزاءً ومصيراً): That is, a reward for their faith and piety, and a destination to which they go and from which they never depart.

Wa'dan mas'ula (وعداً مسؤلا): That is, a promise that is demanded, for the believers demand it, saying, "Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers," and the angels say, "Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You promised them."

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in response to the proposals of the polytheists to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when they said: "Why was not an angel sent down to him, or a treasure cast to him, or a garden given to him from which he could eat?" Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He willed, could give you better than that﴾, that is, than what they proposed, when they said: "Take for yourself from your Lord, after you refused their request to abandon your call and give up your message." ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, through its trees and palaces. ﴿And He could give you palaces﴾, not a single palace as they said. But He did not will that for you in this world, because this is a abode of action, not an abode of recompense, rest and bliss. Your Lord is able to grant you that, but He did not will it, and good lies in what He wills. So be patient. The obstacle to the polytheists' faith was not that you are a human who eats food and walks in the markets, nor that Allah did not send down an angel to you. Rather, the obstacle is their denial of the Hour. The cause of their disbelief and obstinacy is their not believing in the Resurrection and the Recompense. Had they believed in the life to come, they would have sought every means that saves them from its punishment and secures its bliss. ﴿Rather, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, that is, the Resurrection, ﴿a blaze﴾, that is, a blazing fire, or it is a level of the levels of Hell called Sa'ir.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾. This is a description of the Sa'ir: when it sees its people, those of polytheism, wrongdoing and corruption, from a distant place, it rages against them with a rage and roars with a frightful roar, so they hear it and their limbs tremble from it. ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place therein, bound together with their necks in shackles﴾, their hands fastened to their necks with chains. ﴿They call out there for destruction﴾, that is, they cry out at the top of their voices, "Woe to us! Destruction!" Come, for this is the time of your presence. So it is said to them, in disgrace, rebuke and regret: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾ This is the time of your destruction, your humiliation and your punishment. Here Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ to those polytheists who deny the Resurrection and the Recompense: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised?﴾, that is, which Allah the Exalted has promised to His servants who guard against His punishment by believing in Him, His Messenger, and obeying Allah and His Messenger. Certainly the Garden of Eternity is better, and there is no comparison between it and the Sa'ir; this is only a reminder. His saying: ﴿It is for them a reward and a destination﴾, that is, the Garden of Eternity is for the people of faith and piety, as a reward, that is, a recompense, and a destination they reach and never leave. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾, that is, therein are kinds of food, drink, clothing and dwellings. His saying: ﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is, they neither die nor leave. His saying: ﴿It is ever a promise binding upon your Lord that is asked for﴾, that is, your Lord, O Messenger, has bestowed it, and promised it to His righteous servants, a promise they ask Him for, and He fulfils it for them. So they say: ﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 194], and the angels say: ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Ghafir: 8].

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification that the root of the disbelief of disbelievers, the injustice of wrongdoers and the corruption of corrupters lies in their denial of the Resurrection and the Recompense in the Hereafter, for whoever believes in the Last Resurrection hastens to obedience and uprightness.

2- Affirmation of the belief in the Last Resurrection by describing some of what takes place in it of recompense: the Fire and the Garden.

3- The virtue of piety, and that it is the foundation of the matter; whoever believes and fears Allah has earned the lofty ranks. May Allah the Exalted make us among the people of piety and the lofty ranks.

His saying: ﴿It is for them a reward and a destination﴾, that is, the Garden of Eternity is for the people of faith and piety, as a reward, that is, a recompense, and a destination they reach and never leave. His saying: ﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is, they neither die nor leave. 1- Clarification that the root of the disbelief of disbelievers, the injustice of wrongdoers and the corruption of corrupters lies in their denial of the Resurrection and the Recompense in the Hereafter, for whoever believes in the Last Resurrection hastens to obedience and uprightness.

2- Affirmation of the belief in the Last Resurrection by describing some of what takes place in it of recompense: the Fire and the Garden.

3- The virtue of piety, and that it is the foundation of the matter; whoever believes and fears Allah has earned the lofty ranks. May Allah the Exalted make us among the people of piety and the lofty ranks.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verse 21–24:

Explanation of the words:

"Those who do not hope for Our meeting": i.e., those who deny the Resurrection, since the servant's meeting with his Lord takes place on the Day of Resurrection.

"Why were the angels not sent down upon us?": i.e., why were angels not sent down upon us to bear witness for you that you are the Messenger of Allah?

"Or we see our Lord": i.e., so that He would tell us that you are a Messenger and that we must believe in you.

"They have been arrogant within themselves": i.e., concerning their own selves; they saw themselves as the greatest and most mighty of things, out of conceit.

"And they have transgressed with great transgression": i.e., they committed great rebellion, to the point that they demanded the descent of the angels and the sight of the Lord, exalted is He.

"And they say, 'A barrier forbidden'": i.e., the angels will say to them, "Forbidden and utterly prohibited for you is good tidings."

"And We will regard what they did": i.e., We will turn to their corrupt deeds, which were not based on knowledge and sincerity.

"Scattered dust": al-Haba' is the dust seen in a ray of sunlight entering through a window (kuwa).

"And better in resting place": al-Maqil is a place of rest at midday in the days of heat.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the statements of the polytheists of Quraysh, so the Exalted says: ﴿And those who do not hope for Our meeting said﴾, namely those who deny the Resurrection and reject the second life with all its bliss and punishment, ﴿"Why were not angels sent down upon us?"﴾ i.e., why did Allah not send down angels to bear witness to Muhammad's prophethood, ﴿"Or [why] do we not see our Lord?"﴾ so that He would tell us that Muhammad is His Messenger and that we must believe in him and in what he brought and called to. The Exalted said: ﴿They have certainly been arrogant toward themselves and have transgressed with great transgression﴾, i.e., by My might and majesty, these polytheists who deny the Resurrection have been arrogant concerning their own selves, seeing themselves as something great, and they have transgressed, i.e., committed great tyranny, in this statement of theirs, which has no cause but the feeling of pride and great inner rebellion. And His saying ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾, i.e., those whom they demand to descend upon them, that is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿No good tidings that Day for the criminals﴾, i.e., those who committed crimes against themselves, corrupting them with polytheism and wrongdoing. Corruption: ﴿And they will say﴾, i.e., and the angels will say to them, ﴿"A barrier forbidden"﴾, i.e., forbidden and utterly prohibited for you is good tidings; rather, it is for the believers who fear Allah.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will regard what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾, i.e., We will turn to their deeds which were not established upon the principle of faith, sincerity, and conformity to the Law, and We will make them scattered dust like the dust seen in the light of the sun entering through a window or opening, which cannot be grasped in the hand nor touched by the fingers due to its fineness and dispersal. Likewise, their deeds yield them nothing, because of their invalidity and their not being acknowledged.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The companions of Paradise﴾, i.e., its people who qualified for it by faith and piety, ﴿on that Day﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection which the deniers denied, ﴿will be better in residence﴾, i.e., a place of settlement and dwelling, ﴿and best in resting place﴾, i.e., a place of rest from fatigue at midday, i.e., better and best than the polytheistic people of the Fire who denied. In this expression there is an indication that the reckoning may be concluded within half a day of reckoning, since Allah is swift in reckoning.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of the arrogance, transgression, and tyranny of the extremist polytheists of Quraysh.

2- Affirmation of the sight of the angels at the seizing of the soul and on the Day of Resurrection.

3- Negation of good tidings for the criminals and affirmation of them for the believers who fear Allah.

4- The nullification and invalidity of the polytheists' deeds, as they gain nothing from them at all.

5- The conclusion of the believers' reckoning before the half of the Day of Reckoning, whose measure is fifty thousand years.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 25–29:

Explanation of the words:

*Bil-ghamam* (بالغمام): i.e., "from the clouds," which is a thin white cloud like the one that was over the Children of Israel in the wilderness (al-tih).

*Al-mulk* (الملك): i.e., the true sovereignty belongs to God; no kings or owners of the earth retain any dominion over anything or in any matter.

*Ala al-kafirina 'asiran* (على الكافرين عسيراً): i.e., difficult and severe.

*Ya'addu al-zalimu 'ala yadayhi* (يعض الظالم على يديه): i.e., in remorse and regret over what he neglected concerning God.

*Sabilan* (سبيلا): i.e., a path to salvation through faith and obedience.

*Lam attakhidh falanan khalilan* (لم أتخذ فلاناً خليلاً): i.e., "I did not take so-and-so as a close, loving friend," referring to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

*La-qad adallani 'an al-dhikr* (لقد أضلني عن الذكر): i.e., from the Qur'an and what it calls to of faith, monotheism, and righteous deeds.

*Wa-kana al-shaytan* (وكان الشيطان): the devil, both the devil of the jinn and the devil of mankind together.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the manifestations of the Resurrection and to explain the state of those who deny it. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And [remember] the Day﴾, i.e., remember, ﴿when the sky will be split open with clouds﴾, i.e., from the clouds, and the angels will be sent down in descent. That is for the coming of the Lord, blessed and exalted, to judge between people. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿The sovereignty that Day belongs truly to the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., it is established for the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, not for anyone else, nor for the kings and owners of this world. That day was ﴿severe for the disbelievers﴾, one that cannot be endured or borne because of the punishment and terrors it contains. And His saying, ﴿And [remember] the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾, i.e., the polytheist, the disbeliever, is an explanation of the difficulty and severity of the day, when the wrongdoer bites his hands out of remorse, regret, and sorrow over his neglect in the world regarding faith and righteous deeds... He says, "Oh, I wish," i.e., wishing: ﴿I had taken a way with the Messenger﴾, i.e., a path to salvation from the terror of this day, through faith and piety. He calls out again, saying: ﴿Woe to me!﴾, i.e., "O my destruction, come, for this is the time of your presence." He wishes again and says: ﴿Oh, I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend﴾, and he is a devil from mankind or jinn who had been his close companion and ally in the world, so he deceived him and led him astray from guidance. So he says in regret: ﴿He led me away from the Reminder﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, after it had come to me from my Lord through the Messenger, and in it is my guidance and by it is my being guided. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Satan is ever a betrayer of man﴾, i.e., he leads him into ruin, then abandons him and leaves him in various places and situations.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense, by mentioning the resurrection and recompense, its conditions, and some of its terrors.

2- Affirmation that the Lord, blessed and exalted, will come on the Day of Resurrection to judge between people.

3- The remorse and regret of wrongdoers over what they missed of faith and obedience to God and His Messenger.

4- Explanation of the evil consequence of allying with the devils of mankind and jinn and obeying them in disobedience to God and His Messenger.

5- Establishing the principle that the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause, since 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt was the one who obeyed Ubayy ibn Khalaf when he accepted Islam, then Ubayy ibn Khalaf blamed him, so he apostatized from Islam. He is the one who regrets and sorrows, saying: ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend! He led me astray from the Reminder...﴾.

*Ala al-kafirina 'asiran* (على الكافرين عسيراً): i.e., difficult and severe.

*Ya'addu al-zalimu 'ala yadayhi* (يعض الظالم على يديه): i.e., in remorse and regret over what he neglected concerning God.

*Sabilan* (سبيلا): i.e., a path to salvation through faith and obedience.

*Lam attakhidh falanan khalilan* (لم أتخذ فلاناً خليلاً): i.e., "I did not take so-and-so as a close, loving friend," referring to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 30–34:

Explanation of the words:

Mahjūran (مهجوراً): something abandoned and left unattended.

Hādiyan wa naṣīran (هادياً ونصيراً): a guide for you to the path of success and triumph, and a helper for you against all your enemies.

Jumlatan wāḥidah (جملة واحدة): as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms were revealed all at once, without being divided or dispersed.

Li-nuthabbita bihi fu'adak (لنثبت به فؤادك): that We may strengthen your heart so that you can bear the burdens of the message and convey it.

Wa-rattalnāhu tartīlan (ورتلناه ترتيلاً): We revealed it piece by piece, verse after verse and surah after surah, so that it might be easy to understand and to memorize.

Sharru makānan (شر مكاناً): they will be made to go to it, which is Hell, from which we seek refuge with God.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to present the state of the Final Resurrection, which the polytheists denied and rejected. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the Messenger says: "My Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ This is the Messenger's ﷺ complaint about his people to his Lord, so that He may take them to account for it. Their abandonment of the Qur'an means their neglect of listening to it, understanding it, and acting upon what it contains.

As for His saying: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾, meaning: just as We have appointed for you, O Messenger, enemies among the criminals of your people, so We appointed for every prophet before you an enemy from among the criminals of his people. Therefore be patient and endure until you convey your message and fulfill your trust, and your Lord is sufficient as a guide to the way of your success and as a helper against your enemies. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ meaning: the deniers of the Resurrection, the rejecters of Muhammadan prophethood, and the polytheists who associate idols with God said: why was the Qur'an not sent down to him in one go, with its parts together, not divided into separate verses and surahs? That is, just as the Torah was sent down all at once, and likewise the Gospel and the Psalms. This is among their obstinacy and the baseless demands that have no meaning, since this is not their concern, nor is it something they have any right to delve into; rather, it is disbelief and stubbornness. Since this might cause the Messenger ﷺ pain, God responded to them with His saying: ﴿Thus⦆ meaning: We sent it down in this way, in portions and separately, for a lofty wisdom, namely to strengthen your heart and make it firm, for it is like rain: whenever it is sent down, it revives the dead earth and it flourishes; and its descending time after time is more beneficial than rain descending all at once. And His saying: ﴿And We have recited it in measured recitation﴾ meaning: He sent it down in measured portions, little by little, so that it might be easy to memorize, understand, and act upon.

3- Explanation of the wisdom in the Qur'an's revelation in measured, separate portions, little by little.

4- Explanation that the criminals will be gathered upon their faces, not on their feet, to Hell, as humiliation and punishment for them.

3- Explanation of the wisdom in the Qur'an's revelation in measured, separate portions, little by little.

4- Explanation that the criminals will be gathered upon their faces, not on their feet, to Hell, as humiliation and punishment for them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 35–40:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Kitab (the Book): That is, the Torah.

Wazir (helper): That is, one who strengthens his arm, supports him, and bears with him the burdens of the call.

Ila al-qawm alladhina kadhdhabu (to the people who denied): They are Pharaoh and his household.

Lamma kadhdhabu al-rusul (when they denied the messengers): That is, Noah, peace be upon him.

Wa ja'alnahum li-n-nas aya (and We made them a sign for mankind): That is, a sign of Our power in destroying and annihilating the wrongdoers, and a lesson for those who take heed.

Wa 'Adan wa Thamud (and 'Ad and Thamud): That is, mention the people of 'Ad and Thamud, etc.

Wa ashab ar-Rass (and the companions of the Rass): Ar-Rass is a well (rass) in which a people threw their prophet, that is, they cast him into it and buried him in the earth.

Wa qurunan bayna dhalika kathiran (and many generations between those): That is, We destroyed many generations among the nations we have mentioned.

Tabbarna tatbiran (We utterly destroyed): That is, We destroyed them with complete destruction.

Allati umtirat matar as-su' (the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil): It is Sodom, the town of the people of Lot.

La yarjuna nushuran (they did not hope for resurrection): That is, they did not believe in the resurrection and the other recompense.

Meaning of the verses:

The statement of the Exalted, ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾: This begins a presentation of nations that denied their messengers and rejected the call of truth they brought, so God destroyed them, so that this would be an admonition to the polytheists, perhaps they would take heed. God the Exalted said: By Our might, We certainly gave Moses son of 'Imran the Book, which is the Torah. ﴿And We made his brother Aaron with him a helper﴾, that is, a supporter. So We said, that is, to the two of them: ﴿Go to the people who denied Our signs﴾, and they are Pharaoh and his chiefs. They went to them and they denied the two of them, so We destroyed them with complete destruction, as they were drowned in the sea. The statement of the Exalted: ﴿And the people of Noah﴾, that is, mention the people of Noah as well, for when they denied the messengers, that is, they denied Noah, and whoever denies one messenger has, as it were, denied all the messengers, We drowned them by the flood and made them a sign for mankind after them, that is, a lesson for those who take heed. His statement ﴿And We have prepared﴾, that is, We have readied for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter a painful punishment, that is, a grievous one, in addition to the destruction of the world. His statement ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud and the companions of the Rass﴾, that is, We destroyed them all, annihilating them with destruction, because they denied Our messengers and rejected Our call. And generations, that is, We destroyed many generations between those We have mentioned.

His statement ﴿And to each We set forth parables﴾, that is, as the establishment of proof against them; We did not destroy them except after warning and giving them excuse. His statement ﴿And each We utterly destroyed with destruction﴾, that is, We destroyed them with destruction because they denied Our messengers and rejected Our call. His statement: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil﴾, that is, the unbelievers of Quraysh passed by the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil, that is, stones, and it is the towns of the people of Lot: Sodom, Gomorrah and others, so He destroyed them for denying their messenger and committing indecency. The statement of the Exalted: ﴿Have they not been seeing it﴾ during their journeys to Syria and Palestine, ﴿so that they might take heed and believe?﴾ This is a rhetorical interrogation. Even though they were passing by it, they did not take heed, for a reason: they did not believe in the final resurrection, which is the meaning of the statement of the Exalted: ﴿Rather, they did not hope for resurrection﴾. Whoever does not hope to be raised, called to account and recompensed does not believe, and never will he be upright.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of God's way of destroying nations after warning and giving them excuse.

2- Explanation of the end of the deniers and the destruction and punishment that befell them.

3- Explanation of the reason for Quraysh's denial of the Messenger ﷺ and what he brought, which is their denial of the resurrection and recompense; therefore admonitions did not benefit them and lessons did not affect them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 41–44:

Explanation of the words:

*In yatakhidhunaka*: i.e., they take you (only) as... (ma yatakhidhunaka: "they do not take you").

*Illa huzuwan*: i.e., one who is mocked at.

*Ahadha alladhi ba'atha Allahu rasulan*: i.e., regarding his claim, not that they acknowledge his prophethood. The interrogative is one of ridicule and contempt.

*In kada liyudillana 'an alihatina*: i.e., he came close to turning us away from our gods.

*Lawla an sabarna 'alayha*: i.e., he would have turned us away from them.

*Ara'ayta man ittakhadha ilahahu hawahu*: i.e., tell me about the one who made his desire his deity and obeyed his desire. Would you be able to guide him?

*In hum illa ka-al-an'am*: i.e., they are nothing but like cattle in their lack of awareness and perception.

Meaning of the verses:

His Exalted saying, ﴿And when they see you, they take you not but in ridicule﴾, informs His Messenger about those polytheists who deny the Resurrection: when they see him in a gathering or on a road, they take him only as one to be mocked, i.e., made an object of ridicule, out of contempt and disdain for him. They say among themselves, ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ This is a question of contempt and disdain, because they do not believe he is the Messenger of Allah. And they say, ﴿He almost led us astray from our gods﴾, i.e., he almost turned us away from worshipping our gods, had we not been patient and steadfast in worshipping them. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 45–50:

Explanation of the words:

"Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shade" (ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل): That is, have you not looked at the work of your Lord in the shade, how He spread it out?

"And if He willed, He would have made it stationary" (ولو شاء الله لجعله ساكناً): That is, fixed in its state in length and extension, neither shortening nor lengthening.

"Then We made the sun over it an indicator" (ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلاً): That is, a sign of its existence, for were it not for the sun, the shade would not be recognized.

"Then We draw it in to Us, a gradual drawing in" (ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضاً يسيرا): That is, We remove it by the light of the sun slowly, part by part, until it ends.

"Then We made the night a garment" (ثم جعلنا الليل لباساً): That is, it covers you with its darkness as clothing covers you.

"And sleep a rest" (والنوم سباتاً): That is, a rest for your bodies from the toil of the day's work.

"And made the day a resurrection" (وجعل النهار نشوراً): That is, a life, since sleep at night is like death, and dispersal by day is like resurrection.

"As a glad tiding before His mercy" (بشراً بين يدي رحمته): That is, bringing good news of rain before it falls, and the rain is the mercy.

"And We sent down from the sky pure water" (ماء طهوراً): That is, something by which you purify yourselves from ritual impurities and dirt.

"That We may give life thereby to a dead land" (لنحيي به بلدة ميتاً): That is, with various crops and plants.

"And to give drink to cattle and many people" (أنعاماً وأناسي كثيراً): That is, many animals and many people.

"And We have certainly distributed it among them" (ولقد صرفناه بينهم): That is, the rain, so that it falls on the land of one people and does not fall on another, for lofty wisdom.

"That they may remember" (ليذكروا): That is, that they may remember God's favor upon them, thank Him, believe, and affirm His oneness.

"But most of the people refuse except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً): That is, they did not remember, and most of them refused except ingratitude, denying the blessing.

Meaning of the verses:

His statement, Exalted is He, "Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shade" (ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل): This begins the mention of a group of proofs of monotheism, which are manifestations of the lordship of God that necessitate His divinity. First, the shade, which is observed from the time of dawn until sunrise, and which the Creator, mighty and majestic, has extended, that is, spread across the universe. Then the sun rises and begins to diminish and contract it little by little. Had God, Exalted is He, willed, He would have made it stationary, not departing or leaving, but according to the interest of His servants He made it shorten and contract until the sun stands at the middle of the sky, and it becomes still. Then, when the sun declines, inclining toward setting, the shade returns little by little, lengthening gradually, so that by it the hours of the day and the times of prayer are known, until it reaches a great length as it was at the beginning of the day. Then it is drawn in, a gentle, hidden, and swift drawing in, when the sun sets and the darkness of night covers it. This is a sign of God's power, knowledge, wisdom, and mercy toward His servants, manifest in the shade, concerning which He, Exalted is He, said "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), O Messenger, that is, do you not look at the work of your Lord, majestic in His majesty, "how He extends the shade? And had He willed, He would have made it stationary" (ولو شاء لجعله ساكناً), moving not. "Then We made the sun over it an indicator" (ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلاً), for by its light it is known; were it not for the sun, the shade would not be recognized. His statement, Exalted is He, "Then We draw it in to Us, a gradual drawing" (ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضاً يسيراً), according to His way; in complete concealment and total swiftness the shade is entirely withdrawn, and the intense darkness takes its place.

Second: concerning the night and the day, God, Exalted is He, said: "And it is He who made for you the night as a garment" (وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباساً), that is, a covering that conceals you with its darkness as clothes conceal you. "And sleep as a rest" (والنوم سباتاً), that is, He made sleep a cessation of work, through which the bodies attain rest. "And made the day a resurrection" (وجعل النهار نشوراً), that is, a life after death, for sleep is death, and during the day people disperse to seek provision through work, by the means and laws which God has established for that.

Third: the sending of the winds to fertilize the clouds for rain, to give life to the earth after its death through drought and barrenness. God, Exalted is He, said: "And it is He who sends the winds" (وهو الذي أرسل الرياح), He alone, not any other false deity, "sending the winds as glad tidings before His mercy" (أرسل الرياح بشراً بين يدي رحمته), that is, heralds of rain preceding it, and it is the mercy, and they are before His hands. Who does this other than God? O God, there is none.

Fourth: the sending down of pure, sweet, sweet-tasting water for purification, and for drinking by animals and humans. God, Exalted is He, said: "And We sent down from the sky pure water" (وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهوراً), "that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to what We have created of cattle" (لنحيي به بلدة ميتاً ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاماً), that is, camels, cows and sheep, "and many people" (وأناسي كثيراً), that is, many humans, who are the children of Adam. In the creation of water, its sending down, the creation of need for it in animals and humans, and then guiding them to consume and drink it, all this is evidence of lordship which necessitates the oneness of God, Exalted is He.

Fifth: the distribution of rain among people, so that it rains on one land and does not rain on another, according to divine wisdom and divine upbringing. God, Exalted is He, said: "And We have certainly distributed it among them" (ولقد صرفناه بينهم), that is, among people, as is observed: one region is watered while another is deprived. And His statement, Exalted is He, "But most of the people refused except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً), that is, denial of God's bounty upon them, His lordship over them, and His divinity toward them. This is a matter that calls for wonder and astonishment. These are the manifestations of lordship which necessitate divinity, "But most of the people refused except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً), and we seek refuge in God, Exalted is He.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Presenting sensory proofs for the obligation of worshipping God, affirming His oneness in worship, and the obligation of believing in resurrection and recompense, which the polytheists denied, so they went far astray.

2- Explaining the benefit of the shade, for by it the hours of the day are known, and by it the time of the noon and afternoon prayers is known. The time of noon begins with the first increase of shade (al-fay'), meaning the increase of shadow after it stops decreasing when the sun stands at midday, and the time of the afternoon prayer begins when the shadow becomes equal to its object plus the length of the shadow at noon. That is, when noon has entered and the shadow is four feet or three or less or more, then when it increases by an equal amount the afternoon begins. If the sun declines with a shadow of four feet, then the afternoon enters when the shadow is eight feet; if the sun declines with a shadow of three feet, then the afternoon is at six feet, and so on.

3- Pure water, which is that which remains in its original creation, not mixed with anything that changes its taste, color or smell, and by which ritual impurities are lifted and impurities are washed away, and it is forbidden to withhold it from one who needs it for drinking or purification.

"But most of the people refuse except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً): That is, they did not remember, and most of them refused except ingratitude, denying the blessing.

Meaning of the verses:

His statement, Exalted is He, "Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shade" (ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل): This begins the mention of a group of proofs of monotheism, which are manifestations of the lordship of God that necessitate His divinity. First, the shade, which is observed from the time of dawn until sunrise, and which the Creator, mighty and majestic, has extended, that is, spread across the universe. Then the sun rises and begins to diminish and contract it little by little. Had God, Exalted is He, willed, He would have made it stationary, not departing or leaving, but according to the interest of His servants He made it shorten and contract until the sun stands at the middle of the sky, and it becomes still. Then, when the sun declines, inclining toward setting, the shade returns little by little, lengthening gradually, so that by it the hours of the day and the times of prayer are known, until it reaches a great length as it was at the beginning of the day. Then it is drawn in, a gentle, hidden, and swift drawing in, when the sun sets and the darkness of night covers it. This is a sign of God's power, knowledge, wisdom, and mercy toward His servants, manifest in the shade, concerning which He, Exalted is He, said "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), O Messenger, that is, do you not look at the work of your Lord, majestic in His majesty, "how He extends the shade? And had He willed, He would have made it stationary" (ولو شاء لجعله ساكناً), moving not. "Then We made the sun over it an indicator" (ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلاً), for by its light it is known; were it not for the sun, the shade would not be recognized. His statement, Exalted is He, "Then We draw it in to Us, a gradual drawing" (ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضاً يسيراً), according to His way; in complete concealment and total swiftness the shade is entirely withdrawn, and the intense darkness takes its place.

Second: concerning the night and the day, God, Exalted is He, said: "And it is He who made for you the night as a garment" (وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباساً), that is, a covering that conceals you with its darkness as clothes conceal you. "And sleep as a rest" (والنوم سباتاً), that is, He made sleep a cessation of work, through which the bodies attain rest. "And made the day a resurrection" (وجعل النهار نشوراً), that is, a life after death, for sleep is death, and during the day people disperse to seek provision through work, by the means and laws which God has established for that.

Third: the sending of the winds to fertilize the clouds for rain, to give life to the earth after its death through drought and barrenness. God, Exalted is He, said: "And it is He who sends the winds" (وهو الذي أرسل الرياح), He alone, not any other false deity, "sending the winds as glad tidings before His mercy" (أرسل الرياح بشراً بين يدي رحمته), that is, heralds of rain preceding it, and it is the mercy, and they are before His hands. Who does this other than God? O God, there is none.

Fourth: the sending down of pure, sweet, sweet-tasting water for purification, and for drinking by animals and humans. God, Exalted is He, said: "And We sent down from the sky pure water" (وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهوراً), "that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to what We have created of cattle" (لنحيي به بلدة ميتاً ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاماً), that is, camels, cows and sheep, "and many people" (وأناسي كثيراً), that is, many humans, who are the children of Adam. In the creation of water, its sending down, the creation of need for it in animals and humans, and then guiding them to consume and drink it, all this is evidence of lordship which necessitates the oneness of God, Exalted is He.

Fifth: the distribution of rain among people, so that it rains on one land and does not rain on another, according to divine wisdom and divine upbringing. God, Exalted is He, said: "And We have certainly distributed it among them" (ولقد صرفناه بينهم), that is, among people, as is observed: one region is watered while another is deprived. And His statement, Exalted is He, "But most of the people refused except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً), that is, denial of God's bounty upon them, His lordship over them, and His divinity toward them. This is a matter that calls for wonder and astonishment. These are the manifestations of lordship which necessitate divinity, "But most of the people refused except denial" (فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفوراً), and we seek refuge in God, Exalted is He.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Presenting sensory proofs for the obligation of worshipping God, affirming His oneness in worship, and the obligation of believing in resurrection and recompense, which the polytheists denied, so they went far astray.

2- Explaining the benefit of the shade, for by it the hours of the day are known, and by it the time of the noon and afternoon prayers is known. The time of noon begins with the first increase of shade (al-fay'), meaning the increase of shadow after it stops decreasing when the sun stands at midday, and the time of the afternoon prayer begins when the shadow becomes equal to its object plus the length of the shadow at noon. That is, when noon has entered and the shadow is four feet or three or less or more, then when it increases by an equal amount the afternoon begins. If the sun declines with a shadow of four feet, then the afternoon enters when the shadow is eight feet; if the sun declines with a shadow of three feet, then the afternoon is at six feet, and so on.

3- Pure water, which is that which remains in its original creation, not mixed with anything that changes its taste, color or smell, and by which ritual impurities are lifted and impurities are washed away, and it is forbidden to withhold it from one who needs it for drinking or purification.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 25, verses 51–56**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيرًا﴾ (*Had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town*): that is, a messenger to warn its people of the consequences of shirk (associating partners with God) and disbelief.

﴿وَجَاهِدْهُم بِهِ جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا﴾ (*and strive against them with it, a great striving*): that is, with the Qur'an, a great striving in which you exert your utmost effort.

﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ (*He released the two seas*): that is, He mixed them together, while at the same time preventing the salt water from corrupting the sweet water.

﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا﴾ (*and placed between them a barrier*): that is, a barrier between the salt of one and the sweet of the other.

﴿وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا﴾ (*and a forbidding partition*): that is, He placed between them a firm, preventing barrier, so that the salt does not become sweet and the sweet does not become salt.

﴿خَلَقَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ بَشَرًا﴾ (*created from water a human being*): that is, He created man from water, and what is meant by water is the nutfah (the drop of semen).

﴿فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا﴾ (*and made him [into] lineage and marriage*): that is, male and female; lineage by which one is traced, and marriage through which one becomes related by marriage, i.e., one marries.

﴿مَا لَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ (*that which neither benefits them nor harms them*): that is, idols that neither harm nor benefit.

﴿وَكَانَ الْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيرًا﴾ (*and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord*): that is, a helper to Satan in disobedience to the Most Merciful.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context continues to enumerate the manifestations of divine lordship (*rububiyyah*), which necessitate monotheism (*tawhid*). God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town﴾, that is, a warner to every city, a messenger who warns people of the consequences of shirk and disbelief. But We did not will it, for a wisdom required by Our lordship: that you, O Messenger, should be the best of messengers, the greatest in rank and the most abundant in reward. So We bestowed this virtue upon you, and you became the messenger of all the towns, white and black alike. So be patient and endure, and remember the nobility of your station. ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in any matter they desire from you. ﴿And strive against them with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, all of which consists of proofs and clear evidences, ﴿a great striving﴾ in which you exert your utmost effort.

After this parenthetical statement within the divine speech, God, exalted is He, continues to mention the manifestations of His lordship over His creation: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas﴾, the salt and the sweet, that is, He let them flow alongside one another. ﴿This one is sweet and palatable, its drink agreeable, and this one is salty and bitter﴾ [Fatir: 12], that is, undrinkable. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier and a forbidding partition﴾, that is, a concealing, preventing barrier against the mixing of the sweet with the salt, despite their being in one place, so that neither transgresses upon the other by making the salt sweet or the sweet salty.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being﴾, that is, from the seminal fluid and its drop He created man, and made him male and female. This is the meaning of His saying "lineage and marriage": that is, those with lineage to whom one is traced, who are the males, and those with marriage through whom one becomes related by marriage, who are the females. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾, that is, capable of doing whatever He wills of creation and bringing into being, or of transformation and alteration, and of taking away and giving.

These are the manifestations of lordship that necessitate His worship and His oneness. Yet the polytheists worship other than Him, idols that neither benefit them if they worship them nor harm them if they do not. They do so out of their ignorance and the darkness of their souls, so they worship Satan, for it is he who adorned for them the worship of idols. Thus the disbeliever is a helper against his Lord, for by worshipping Satan he assists him in disobeying the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: "and they worship besides God that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord."

That is, a helper to Satan against the Most Merciful, and we seek refuge with God, exalted is He.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. God says to His Messenger: We did not send you except to bring good news to the believers of Paradise and to warn the disbelievers of the Fire. As for guiding hearts, that is up to Us: whomever We will to guide is guided, and whomever We do not will to guide goes astray. Indeed God guides and leads astray according to patterns (*sunan*) of His which have been mentioned many times before.

**Lessons from the verses:**

1. An indication of the wisdom in there being no multiplicity of messengers in the era of the Muhammadan mission, and in being satisfied with the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

2. The prohibition of obeying disbelievers in matters of religion and the sharia.

3. Among striving (*jihad*) is striving against disbelievers and atheists with Qur'anic proofs and revealed verses.

4. Manifestations of God's knowledge and power in the non-mixing of the two seas despite their being in one place; and in God's creation of man from water and making him male and female for procreation and the preservation of the species.

5. Condemnation of the polytheists and disbelievers who assist Satan against the Most Merciful.

**Explanation of the words:**

*ʿalayhi min ajr* (ﷺ... no): That is, for conveying the message, I ask of you no reward that I would seek from you.

*wa-sabbiḥ biḥamdihi* (and glorify Him with His praise): That is, say, "Glory be to God, and praise be to Him."

*fī sittati ayyām* (in six days): That is, of the days of this world which He determined, and they are Sunday... to Friday.

*thumma istawā ʿalā al-ʿarsh* (then He established Himself upon the Throne): *al-ʿarsh* is the throne of sovereignty. The *istiwāʾ* (establishment) is known, the *kayf* (modality) is unknown, and belief in it is obligatory.

*fasʾal bihi khabīran* (then ask about Him one who is well-informed): That is, O human, ask one who is informed about the Throne of the Most Merciful, and he will inform you, for it is great.

*wa-zādahum nufūran* (and it increased them in aversion): That is, the saying to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful," increased them in aversion to faith.

*jaʿala fī al-samāʾ burūjan* (He placed in the sky constellations): they are twelve constellations; see their detail in the explanation of the verses.

*sirājan* (a lamp): that is, the sun.

*khilfah* (alternation): that is, each of them succeeds the other, as is observed.

*an yadhdhakkara* (that he may remember): that is, whatever one has missed in one of them, one does in the other.

*aw arāda shukūran* (or desired gratitude): that is, gratitude for the blessings of his Lord upon him in both of them, through fasting and prayer.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After this great presentation of the manifestations of Lordship, which necessitate worship of Him alone, God Almighty commanded His Messenger to say to the polytheists: "I do not ask you for any wage for this clarification which I have made to you, by which you may know your true God, so that you worship Him and are guided to His worship, and [thereby] gain (*tusʿidūn*) a reward, meaning wealth." But whoever wishes to spend from his wealth in the ways of righteousness and goodness, seeking nearness to his Lord thereby, may do so, so that by his spending in the way of God he takes a path to his Lord's good pleasure and His mercy toward him.

As for His saying ﴿And rely upon the Living, who does not die﴾: God Almighty commands His Messenger to continue on the path of his call, conveying from his Lord, calling to Him, relying upon Him, that is, entrusting his affair to Him, since He is the Living who does not die while others die. He commanded him to seek help in his call and in his patience upon it through glorification, so He said ﴿and glorify Him with His praise﴾, that is, say, "Glory be to God and praise be to Him," and "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You." This is a command to remembrance, prayer, and all other acts of worship, for they are a great help to the servant in steadfastness and patience. As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾: that is, do not be distressed for them or grieve over them because of their disbelief, denial, and polytheism, for your Lord knows their sins and will count their deeds against them and will recompense them for them, in their immediate affair or their later affair. Then Blessed and Exalted is He praised Himself by His saying ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, measured by the days of this world, the first of which is Sunday and the last of which is Friday, ﴿then established Himself upon the great Throne﴾ in an establishment befitting His majesty and perfection. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾, whose mercy encompasses all the worlds. ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾: that is, so ask, O Muhammad, about the Most Merciful one who is informed of His creation, for He is the Creator of everything and the Knower of everything. He alone is the Knower of the greatness of His Throne, the vastness of His dominion, and the majesty and perfection of His essence. There is no god but Him, and no lord other than Him.

As for His saying ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful"﴾: that is, when the Messenger says to them, "O polytheists, prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful, and do not prostrate to anything else among the creatures." They said, denying and feigning ignorance, ﴿"And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾, that is, "Do you wish to impose your obedience upon us?" ﴿And it increased them﴾ this saying ﴿in aversion﴾, that is, in distance from and rejection of the truth, and we seek refuge in God Almighty.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾: that is, He is sanctified and exalted above having a partner in His creation or in His worship, He who by His greatness placed in the sky constellations, which are the stations of the seven wandering planets; these were named *burūj* (constellations), plural of *burj*, which is a great palace. These twelve constellations are known as Aries (*al-Ḥamal*), Taurus (*al-Thawr*), Gemini (*al-Jawzāʾ*), Cancer (*al-Saraṭān*), Leo (*al-Asad*), Virgo (*al-Sunbulah*), Libra (*al-Mīzān*), Scorpio (*al-ʿAqrab*), Sagittarius (*al-Qaws*), Capricorn (*al-Jadī*), Aquarius (*al-Dalw*), and Pisces (*al-Ḥūt*). The seven wandering planets are: Mars (*al-Mirrīkh*), Venus (*al-Zuhara*), Mercury (*ʿUṭārid*), the Moon, the Sun, Jupiter (*al-Mushtarī*), and Saturn (*Zuḥal*). These planets descend into the constellations as into palaces belonging to them.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and placed therein a lamp﴾, which is the sun, ﴿and a illuminating moon﴾, which is the moon, that is, exalted and sanctified is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and an illuminating moon. As for His saying ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day in succession﴾, that is, each of them succeeds the other, so they never coincide. In that are benefits and advantages beyond measure. Among them: whoever forgets a deed during the day remembers it at night and performs it, and whoever forgets a deed at night remembers it during the day and performs it. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾, and His saying ﴿or desires gratitude﴾. For night and day are two containers for worship: fasting by day and standing in prayer by night. Whoever wishes to thank God Almighty for His blessings, He has granted him an opportunity for that: the night for *tahajjud* (voluntary night prayer) and standing, and the day for *jihad* and fasting.

He commanded him to seek help in his call and in his patience upon it through glorification, so He said ﴿and glorify Him with His praise﴾, that is, say, "Glory be to God and praise be to Him," and "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You." This is a command to remembrance, prayer, and all other acts of worship, for they are a great help to the servant in steadfastness and patience. As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾: that is, do not be distressed for them or grieve over them because of their disbelief, denial, and polytheism, for your Lord knows their sins and will count their deeds against them and will recompense them for them, in their immediate affair or their later affair. Then Blessed and Exalted is He praised Himself by His saying ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, measured by the days of this world, the first of which is Sunday and the last of which is Friday, ﴿then established Himself upon the great Throne﴾ in an establishment befitting His majesty and perfection. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾, whose mercy encompasses all the worlds. ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾: that is, so ask, O Muhammad, about the Most Merciful one who is informed of His creation, for He is the Creator of everything and the Knower of everything. He alone is the Knower of the greatness of His Throne, the vastness of His dominion, and the majesty and perfection of His essence. There is no god but Him, and no lord other than Him.

As for His saying ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful"﴾: that is, when the Messenger says to them, "O polytheists, prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful, and do not prostrate to anything else among the creatures." They said, denying and feigning ignorance, ﴿"And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾, that is, "Do you wish to impose your obedience upon us?" ﴿And it increased them﴾ this saying ﴿in aversion﴾, that is, in distance from and rejection of the truth, and we seek refuge in God Almighty.

These twelve constellations are known as Aries (*al-Ḥamal*), Taurus (*al-Thawr*), Gemini (*al-Jawzāʾ*), Cancer (*al-Saraṭān*), Leo (*al-Asad*), Virgo (*al-Sunbulah*), Libra (*al-Mīzān*), Scorpio (*al-ʿAqrab*), Sagittarius (*al-Qaws*), Capricorn (*al-Jadī*), Aquarius (*al-Dalw*), and Pisces (*al-Ḥūt*). This is the meaning of His saying ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾, and His saying ﴿or desires gratitude﴾. For night and day are two containers for worship: fasting by day and standing in prayer by night. Whoever wishes to thank God Almighty for His blessings, He has granted him an opportunity for that: the night for *tahajjud* (voluntary night prayer) and standing, and the day for *jihad* and fasting.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The call to God should not be accompanied by the caller taking any wage from those he calls to God. Whoever wishes to volunteer from himself and spend in the way of God, that is permitted for him.

2. The obligation of *tawakkul* (reliance) upon God, for He is the Living who does not die while others die.

3. The obligation of glorification, remembrance, and worship, which are the servant's provision, his preparation, and his help.

4. The legislation of prostration at His saying "and it increased them in aversion" for the reciter and the listener.

5. The attribute of the Most Merciful's establishment upon His Throne: it must be affirmed, in a manner befitting God's majesty and perfection, and it is forbidden to interpret it (*taʾwīl*) as domination (*istīlāʾ*), subjugation, or the like.

6. Encouragement to remembrance and gratitude, and seizing opportunities for worship and obedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verse 63–71:

Explanation of the words:

﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾ (yamshoona ʿala al-ard hawnan): with tranquility and dignity.

﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ﴾ (wa-idha khatabahumu al-jahiluna): that is, with words they dislike.

﴿قَالُوا سَلَامًا﴾ (qaluu salaman): that is, words by which they are safe from sin; this is called salam al-mutarakah (the greeting of disengagement).

﴿سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا﴾ (sujjadan wa-qiyaman): that is, they pray at night, prostrating (sujjad, plural of sajid).

﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا﴾ (inna ʿadhabaha kana gharaman): that is, the punishment of Hell is constant, never leaving its companion.

﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ (innaha saat mustaqarran wa-muqaman): that is, how evil it is as a place of settling and dwelling.

﴿لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ (lam yusrifu wa-lam yaqturu): that is, they did not squander and did not stint.

﴿وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾ (wa-kana bayna dhalika qawaman): that is, a middle course between extravagance and stinginess.

﴿الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ (allati harrama Allah): namely every human soul, except the soul of the disbelieving combatant.

﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ (illa bi-al-haqq): this is one of three: disbelief after belief, or adultery after being married (ihsan), or unjust and aggressive killing.

﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾ (yalqa athaman): that is, a severe punishment.

﴿يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ﴾ (yubaddilu Allahu sayyiatihim hasanat): by erasing through repentance the past sins, and establishing in their place the subsequent acts of obedience.

The meaning of the verses:

When the polytheists denied the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), saying ﴿وَمَا الرَّحْمَٰنُ﴾ [al-Furqan: 60] and refused to prostrate to the Most Merciful, and said that Muhammad forbids us from associating partners with God while he calls upon "the Most Merciful" alongside God, saying "O Allah, O Most Merciful," it was fitting, in response to their ignorance of this name, to describe to them the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, so that they might know the Most Merciful through His servants, in line with the saying (the best of you is he who, when seen, reminds one of Allah). So He, the Exalted, said ﴿وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَٰنِ﴾ and described them with eight attributes, and informed about what He has prepared for them of honour on the Day of Resurrection.

The first, in His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾: that is, they are not tyrannical arrogant people, nor disobedient corrupters; rather they walk humbly, upon them tranquility and dignity. ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ﴾: that is, the foolish, with what they dislike of speech, they say words by which they are safe from sin; so they do not repay an evil deed with an evil deed, but with a good one.

The second, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا﴾: that is, they spend their night between prostration and standing, placing their feet together and shedding tears upon their cheeks out of fear of the punishment of their Lord.

The third, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: due to the strength of their certainty, it is as if they feel the flame of Hell approaching their faces, so they say ﴿رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا﴾: that is, persistent and constant, never leaving its companion. ﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾: that is, Hell ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾: that is, how evil it is as a place of settling and dwelling.

The fourth, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا﴾ in their spending, so that they do not exceed the required limit, and ﴿لَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ so that they do not fall short of what is obligatory upon them; their spending between extravagance and stinginess is ﴿قَوَامًا﴾: that is, a just middle course.

The fifth: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ﴾: that is, they do not ask anyone other than their Lord to fulfil their needs, just as they do not associate anyone with the worship of their Lord. ﴿وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ killing it, namely every human soul apart from the soul of the disbelieving combatant, which is permitted to be killed and not forbidden. ﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ which is one of three matters the Messenger ﷺ explained in the hadith of the Two Sahihs:

"The blood of a Muslim man may not be lawfully shed except in one of three cases: the married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community."

﴿وَلَا يَزْنُونَ﴾: that is, they do not commit the grave sin of fornication (zina), and zina is marriage without the conditions of lawful marriage. His saying ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ﴾ is a parenthetical statement between the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful. That is: whoever does what was mentioned of association by calling upon other than the Lord, or killing a soul without right, or fornication, ﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾: that is, punishment, ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ﴾: that is, in the punishment, ﴿مُهَانًا﴾: humiliated and abased. His saying ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ﴾ from polytheism and believed in God, in meeting Him, in His Messenger and in what he brought of the true religion, ﴿وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ such as establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan and performing the Hajj to the Sacred House of God. ﴿فَأُولَٰئِكَ﴾ those mentioned, that is, the repentant, ﴿يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ﴾: that is, God erases their evil deeds through their repentance and records in their place the righteous deeds and acts of obedience after their repentance. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾: that is, He is forgiving toward the repentant among His servants, merciful toward them, so He does not punish them after they have repented. His saying ﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ﴾ refers to someone other than those mentioned, that is, one who returns to God after falling into sins, ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ after his repentance, ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا﴾: that is, he returns to Him, the Exalted, with an acceptable and good return, and so He honours him and bestows favour upon him in the abode of His honour.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Clarification of the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, through whom the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, is known.

2. The virtue of humility and tranquility in walking, and dignity.

3. The virtue of repaying evil with good and of speech free from sin.

4. The virtue of night prayer and fear of the punishment of the Fire.

5. The virtue of moderation and balance in spending, which is the good between two evils.

6. The prohibition of polytheism, killing a soul, and adultery, and that these are the greatest of major sins.

7. Repentance erases what came before it, and an exhortation to repentance, and that it is accepted as long as the dying person has not reached the death rattle.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verse 63–71:

Explanation of the words:

﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾ (yamshoona ʿala al-ard hawnan): with tranquility and dignity.

﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ﴾ (wa-idha khatabahumu al-jahiluna): that is, with words they dislike.

﴿قَالُوا سَلَامًا﴾ (qaluu salaman): that is, words by which they are safe from sin; this is called salam al-mutarakah (the greeting of disengagement).

﴿سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا﴾ (sujjadan wa-qiyaman): that is, they pray at night, prostrating (sujjad, plural of sajid).

﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا﴾ (inna ʿadhabaha kana gharaman): that is, the punishment of Hell is constant, never leaving its companion.

﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ (innaha saat mustaqarran wa-muqaman): that is, how evil it is as a place of settling and dwelling.

﴿لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ (lam yusrifu wa-lam yaqturu): that is, they did not squander and did not stint.

﴿وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾ (wa-kana bayna dhalika qawaman): that is, a middle course between extravagance and stinginess.

﴿الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ (allati harrama Allah): namely every human soul, except the soul of the disbelieving combatant.

﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ (illa bi-al-haqq): this is one of three: disbelief after belief, or adultery after being married (ihsan), or unjust and aggressive killing.

﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾ (yalqa athaman): that is, a severe punishment.

﴿يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ﴾ (yubaddilu Allahu sayyiatihim hasanat): by erasing through repentance the past sins, and establishing in their place the subsequent acts of obedience.

The meaning of the verses:

When the polytheists denied the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), saying ﴿وَمَا الرَّحْمَٰنُ﴾ [al-Furqan: 60] and refused to prostrate to the Most Merciful, and said that Muhammad forbids us from associating partners with God while he calls upon "the Most Merciful" alongside God, saying "O Allah, O Most Merciful," it was fitting, in response to their ignorance of this name, to describe to them the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, so that they might know the Most Merciful through His servants, in line with the saying (the best of you is he who, when seen, reminds one of Allah). So He, the Exalted, said ﴿وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَٰنِ﴾ and described them with eight attributes, and informed about what He has prepared for them of honour on the Day of Resurrection.

The first, in His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾: that is, they are not tyrannical arrogant people, nor disobedient corrupters; rather they walk humbly, upon them tranquility and dignity. ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ﴾: that is, the foolish, with what they dislike of speech, they say words by which they are safe from sin; so they do not repay an evil deed with an evil deed, but with a good one.

The second, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا﴾: that is, they spend their night between prostration and standing, placing their feet together and shedding tears upon their cheeks out of fear of the punishment of their Lord.

The third, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: due to the strength of their certainty, it is as if they feel the flame of Hell approaching their faces, so they say ﴿رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا﴾: that is, persistent and constant, never leaving its companion. ﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾: that is, Hell ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾: that is, how evil it is as a place of settling and dwelling.

The fourth, in His saying ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا﴾ in their spending, so that they do not exceed the required limit, and ﴿لَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ so that they do not fall short of what is obligatory upon them; their spending between extravagance and stinginess is ﴿قَوَامًا﴾: that is, a just middle course.

The fifth: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ﴾: that is, they do not ask anyone other than their Lord to fulfil their needs, just as they do not associate anyone with the worship of their Lord. ﴿وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ killing it, namely every human soul apart from the soul of the disbelieving combatant, which is permitted to be killed and not forbidden. ﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ which is one of three matters the Messenger ﷺ explained in the hadith of the Two Sahihs:

"The blood of a Muslim man may not be lawfully shed except in one of three cases: the married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community."

﴿وَلَا يَزْنُونَ﴾: that is, they do not commit the grave sin of fornication (zina), and zina is marriage without the conditions of lawful marriage. His saying ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ﴾ is a parenthetical statement between the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful. That is: whoever does what was mentioned of association by calling upon other than the Lord, or killing a soul without right, or fornication, ﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾: that is, punishment, ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ﴾: that is, in the punishment, ﴿مُهَانًا﴾: humiliated and abased. His saying ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ﴾ from polytheism and believed in God, in meeting Him, in His Messenger and in what he brought of the true religion, ﴿وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ such as establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan and performing the Hajj to the Sacred House of God. ﴿فَأُولَٰئِكَ﴾ those mentioned, that is, the repentant, ﴿يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ﴾: that is, God erases their evil deeds through their repentance and records in their place the righteous deeds and acts of obedience after their repentance. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾: that is, He is forgiving toward the repentant among His servants, merciful toward them, so He does not punish them after they have repented. His saying ﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ﴾ refers to someone other than those mentioned, that is, one who returns to God after falling into sins, ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ after his repentance, ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا﴾: that is, he returns to Him, the Exalted, with an acceptable and good return, and so He honours him and bestows favour upon him in the abode of His honour.

﴿الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ (allati harrama Allah): namely every human soul, except the soul of the disbelieving combatant.

1. Clarification of the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, through whom the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, is known.

2. The virtue of humility and tranquility in walking, and dignity.

3. The virtue of repaying evil with good and of speech free from sin.

4. The virtue of night prayer and fear of the punishment of the Fire.

5. The virtue of moderation and balance in spending, which is the good between two evils.
