Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 25, verses 72–77:

Explanation of the words:

"لا يشهدون الزور" (They do not bear witness to falsehood): that is, they do not attend gatherings of falsehood, and they do not testify to lies and vanity.

"وإذا مروا باللغو" (And when they pass by vain talk): that is, by evil and ugly speech, and everything that contains no good.

"مروا كراماً" (They pass by with dignity): that is, turning away from it, honouring themselves by not listening to it or taking part in it.

"وإذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم" (And when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord): that is, when they are admonished with the verses of the Qur'an.

"لم يخروا عليها صماً وعمياناً" (They do not fall upon them deaf and blind): that is, they do not bow their heads when hearing them, as if blind and unable to see, or deaf and unable to hear. Rather, they attend closely, hearing and understanding what they call to, and seeing what they display.

"قرة أعين" (Comfort of the eyes): that is, that which gladdens our eyes, which is to see them obedient to You, worshipping You alone.

"واجعلنا للمتقين إماماً" (And make us an example for the God-fearing): that is, among Your servants who guard against Your wrath by obeying You, a model whom they may follow in good.

"يجزون الغرفة" (They will be rewarded with the lofty chamber): that is, the highest rank in Paradise.

"بما صبروا" (For what they endured patiently): that is, in obedience to You, by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

"حسنت مستقراً ومقاماً" (How good it is as a place of rest and dwelling): that is, how excellent and pleasant it is as a place of settlement and residence.

"ما يعبأ بكم ربي" (My Lord would not care for you): that is, He does not heed, value or concern Himself with you.

"لولا دعاؤكم" (Were it not for your calling upon Him): that is, your invocation of Him, and His calling you to worship Him through remembrance and thanks.

"فسوف يكون لزاماً" (Then it will be inevitable): that is, the punishment will be inescapable for you, at Badr and on the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues describing the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, which the polytheists ignored when they said: "And what is the Most Merciful?" Here are the attributes of His servants, indicating Him and His majesty and perfection. Five attributes have already been mentioned:

The sixth: in His saying, ﴿And those who do not bear witness to falsehood﴾. Falsehood (zur) is vanity and lying, and the servants of the Most Merciful do not attend its gatherings, do not utter it, do not witness it, and do not speak it. ﴿And when they pass by vain talk﴾, which is every deed and word that contains no good, ﴿they pass by with dignity﴾, that is, honouring themselves by avoiding being soiled by it or falling into it.

The seventh: in His saying, ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord﴾, that is, when anyone reminds them of the verses of the Qur'an, the Book of their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿they do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾, so as not to hear its admonitions, and not blind so as not to see the effects of its signs. Rather, they bow their heads while listening, understanding what it says and calls to, seeing its effects, witnessing its events, and being moved by them.

The eighth: in His saying, ﴿And those who say﴾, that is, in their supplication, ﴿"Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes"﴾, that is, that which gladdens our eyes, by seeing them learn guidance and act upon it, seeking Your pleasure, O our Lord. ﴿And make us an example for the God-fearing﴾ among Your servants who guard against Your wrath by obeying You, by carrying out Your command and the command of Your Messenger, and avoiding Your prohibition and the prohibition of Your Messenger, ﴿and make us an example for the God-fearing﴾, that is, a righteous model whom they may follow in good, O our Lord. Almighty God, informing of them concerning what He bestowed upon them, said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the lofty of soul and exalted of spirit, ﴿will be rewarded with the lofty chamber﴾, which is the highest rank in Paradise, ﴿for what they endured patiently﴾ in obedience to their Master, and for the harm that befell them for the sake of their Lord, ﴿and they will be met therein﴾, that is, the angels will receive them with greetings and salutations, ﴿with greeting and peace﴾, that is, with prayers for a happy life and safety from calamities, for it is a life without death and a happiness without troubles.

His saying, ﴿abiding therein﴾, that is, in that chamber at the highest part of Paradise, ﴿how good it is as a place of rest and dwelling﴾, that is, how excellent a place of settlement and residence. Up to here the discussion of the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful and the explanation of their reward with their Lord has ended.

His saying: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your calling upon Him"﴾, that is, say, O our Messenger, to those polytheists who deny the Most Merciful: ﴿"My Lord would not care for you"﴾, that is, He would not concern Himself with you or value you, ﴿were it not for your calling upon Him﴾, that is, the worship of those among you who worship Him, for supplication is worship. I would not care for you nor concern myself with you. But since you have denied Me and My Messenger, and have not worshipped Me nor affirmed My oneness, then ﴿it will be inevitable﴾ that the punishment will come upon you, ﴿and it will be inescapable﴾. You have already tasted it at Badr, and it will cling to them in their graves until their resurrection, and it will pursue them until their final abode in Hell.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of bearing false witness and the prohibition of giving testimony for it.

2- The virtue of turning away from vain talk, whether in deed or in word.

3- The virtue of reflecting upon the Qur'an, listening well to its recitation, taking admonition from its exhortations, and acting upon its guidance.

4- The virtue of lofty aspiration, nobility of spirit, and seeking perfection and exemplary conduct in good.

5- Humans, though the noblest of creatures, have no worth unless they worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; if they do not worship Him, they are the worst of creation.
